 U.S. news DOJ charges former Penn State student at center of fraternity drug bust
 Agostino Abbatiello, 24, was accused by federal prosecutors of selling cocaine and recruiting other students to package the illicit drug for sale. Listen to this article with a free profile 00:00 00:00 Agostino Abbatiello, who is facing charges including possession with intent to deliver and conspiracy, arrives for an appearance at Centre County Courthouse in Bellefonte, Pa., on Sept. 2. Matt Rourke / AP Share Add NBC News to Google Nov. 18, 2026, 1:40 PM EST By Matt Lavietes The Justice Department on Wednesday filed criminal charges against a former Pennsylvania State University fraternity brother who prosecutors say was at the center of a drug trafficking ring at the university.
 Agostino Abbatiello, 24, of Westbury, New York, was charged with one count of conspiracy to distribute cocaine and six counts of distributing cocaine, the Justice Department said in a news release. The maximum penalty under federal law for this offense is life in prison, according to the DOJ. 
 Federal prosecutors alleged that between January 2023 and December 2024, Abbatiello was a “major supplier” of cocaine to fraternities at Penn State.
 Abbatiello, a former member of Sigma Chi, sold cocaine in bulk quantities on numerous occasions to the Sigma Chi and Delta Upsilon fraternities, often as much as a kilogram at a time, according to officials. 
 Accused Penn State cocaine ring leader granted $250K bail 01:58 Abbatiello purchased cocaine from suppliers in Philadelphia and New York, officials said. He also recruited others to assist him in obtaining his supply and transporting it to State College, where he used other fraternity brothers and pledges to package the illicit drugs for resale, according to officials. 
 “This defendant was the top rung of the ladder for a high-level drug trafficking ring that supplied cocaine to Penn State University students,” Pennsylvania Attorney General Dave Sunday said in the release.
 A lawyer for Abbatiello did not immediately return a request for comment. 
 Wyatt DuBois, a spokesperson for Penn State, referred NBC News to the Justice Department.
 The university has previously said it has not officially recognized Sigma Chi for years. Sigma Chi’s national organization said it suspended its state chapter after the allegations were made public. 
 Hours after the DOJ charged Abbatiello, Penn State announced that it will no longer recognize the other fraternity alleged to be involved in the alleged drug ring, Delta Upsilon.

 Slide 1 of 1 Penn State said it found evidence that Delta Upsilon members committed acts of hazing that “included extensive control over daily activities, acts of servitude, sleep deprivation, physical punishment, intimidation, humiliation and threats of additional harm.” 
 A representative for Delta Upsilon’s national body did not immediately return a request for comment.
 In August, state authorities had already arrested and charged Abbatiello in connection with the alleged scheme; he was charged with felony corrupt organizations, conspiracy and dealing in proceeds of unlawful activity.
 Thirteen other people were arrested in connection with the alleged drug scheme, including current and former students and the father of a former student.
 Abbatiello posted bail set at $250,000 in connection with his state charges and was released from Pennsylvania detention as he awaits further proceedings.
